subject: Capacity scenario simulations for Cobalt renewal & onboarding window
messages:
From: Harper Lee <harper@cobalt.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity planning for renewal - Cobalt AI

Hi Vivek / Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our renewal for Dedicated capacity is coming up in December and we
need a concrete sizing plan tied to actual usage. Over the last 90 days our median GPU utilization is 
~58% but we've seen three weekend spikes where tail QPS doubled for 6–12 hours (attached summary).
Those spikes are customer-impacting and we need an approach that balances unit cost with risk —
something we can present to our ops and procurement teams.

Specific asks:
- Can you run scenario simulations that map commit tranches (reserved GPUs) vs burst buffers and show cost/SLO tradeoffs?
- We want options at three confidence bands: 60th, 80th, 95th percentile of expected traffic.
- Can you recommend a rollout window (region-by-region) if we convert burst to reserved capacity? We prefer minimal disruption and a pre-warm strategy if needed.

Attaching the CSV we exported from our telemetry. Happy to hop on a quick 30-min call this week.

Thanks,
Harper
Head of Platform
Cobalt AI

Attachments: cobalt-usage-spikes-logs.zip (log-summary)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Harper Lee <harper@cobalt.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning for renewal - Cobalt AI

Harper — appreciate the data. We're running a small simulation sweep now; initial notes below while the workbook builds:

- Baseline: your median 58% utilization maps to ~95 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs for steady-state workloads at your current QPS.
- Weekend spike handling: two approaches — (A) keep burst credits and pre-warm a small reserved tranche (20%) the Friday before expected spikes; (B) convert incremental burst to a thin reserved tranche with autoscale hooks.
- Confidence bands: I’ll produce three headroom layouts (60/80/95) with the expected marginal cost per token and the SLO breach probability.

I attached a working workbook plus a proposed rollout schedule draft for a phased conversion (region-first - west->east).
Can we schedule a 30-min session tomorrow to walk through the sims? If you prefer, I can share a short video walkthrough first.

Vivek
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity-simulations-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), proposed-rollout-schedule.pdf (pdf)

From: Harper Lee <harper@cobalt.ai>

Cc: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@cobalt.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning for renewal - Cobalt AI

Thanks Vivek — tomorrow works. Quick clarifications before the call:
- Spikes are typically 6–10 hours, Saturday nights in US-west (19:00–05:00 PST window). They correlate with a marketing batch and a downstream partner outage that multiplies inference rate.
- We care more about 99.5th token latency than overall cost for those windows. For steady-state weekdays cost is the primary metric.
- We have a hard procurement deadline: budget signoff by 2026-12-15. Any commit needs to be accompanied by concrete mitigation and rollback plan.

Sam will join the call from ops. See you tomorrow at 10:30 PT.

—Harper

Date: 2026-11-03T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Capacity planning for Cobalt - recommended rollout & tranche conversion

Forwarding Harper's data and initial ask. Summary and recommended approach (action items below):

Executive summary:
- Recommendation: convert 25% of Cobalt's burst buffer into a reserved tranche and split the remainder into a 2-week pre-warm window plus burst credits. This yields a projected 3x reduction in 99.5th SLO breach probability during weekend spikes at ~+12% monthly committed cost.
- Phased regional rollout: US-West -> US-East -> APAC (if they expand). Each region conversion will be done in a rolling 48-hour window with pre-warm ramps 36 hours prior.
- Tranche sizing: initial tranche add = 24 GPUs (A100-equivalent), with two subsequent tranches of 48 GPUs and 48 GPUs spaced 30/60 days. This spreads financial impact and provides early telemetry.
- Pre-warm policy: warm KV-cache and prefix caching by replaying a 6-hour sampled workload from prior spikes; TTL controls to avoid long-term cache pollution.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: unexpected multi-region simultaneous spike — Mitigation: keep a small cross-region burst reserve (10%) + fast-fallback to higher-cost ephemeral hosts.
- Risk: procurement lag — Mitigation: draft addendum for incremental tranches as an appendix to the renewal, with explicit rollback clause.

Action items: 
- Kimberly: confirm contract language we can offer for tranche addendum and pricing delta (+12% committed).
- Aditya: validate runtime pre-warm steps and sign off on the 36-hour preload procedure (we'll provide a dry-run on staging).
- Marissa: confirm operational runbook and telemetry alerts to watch 99.5th latency during each tranche activation.

I attached the simulation workbook and the proposed rollout schedule for details. I'll be on the call with Harper tomorrow.

Vivek

Attachments: capacity-simulations-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), proposed-rollout-schedule.pdf (pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T17:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Capacity planning for Cobalt - recommended rollout & tranche conversion

All — this looks reasonable and I approve the high-level approach. A few notes: 

- Legal/Finance: we can do an addendum with staggered tranche commits tied to usage gates. I asked finance for a draft term sheet reflecting +12% committed cost; they prefer the tranches be measured monthly (not daily).
- Pricing: agree to the 24/48/48 tranche split. We'll price the first tranche at the committed rate and provide clear burst-to-reserve conversion math in the addendum.
- Ops: Marissa, please draft the runbook sections for rollback conditions (SLO breach rate > 1.5% for 2 consecutive sampling windows) and include a test plan for the pre-warm procedure.

I'll loop in Legal once finance shares the term sheet. If everyone signs off by EOD Friday we can present to Harper's procurement on 2026-11-10.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Renewals | Redwood Inference
